Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾

They said in its explanation: they do not fear the events of Allah concerning them, like His events concerning those before them among the nations.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 45, verse 21:

He, glory be to Him, denounced this assumption (ḥusbān) with a denunciation that alerts the intellect to its ugliness, and to the fact that it is an evil judgment, and that the one who makes such a judgment is a wrongdoer and an evildoer. Had its ugliness been due merely to its being contrary to what He had informed of, the denunciation would not be for what it entailed of the necessary ugliness of equating the good-doer with the evil-doer, an ugliness established in the natural disposition (fiṭar) of all the worlds. Nor would there be here an evil judgment in itself that is denounced against the one who issues it.

(Fāʾida)

Tamīm al-Dārī recited Surat al-Jāthiya one night, and when he reached this verse, ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds?﴾, he kept repeating it and weeping until morning.

Abū ʿUbayda ʿĀmir ibn al-Jarrāḥ said: "I wish I were a ram, that my family would slaughter me, eat my meat, and sip my broth."

This is a topic whose tracing would be lengthy.

Al-Bukhārī said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: "Chapter: the believer's fear that his deeds may be nullified while he is unaware."

Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: "I never presented my words against my deeds without fearing that I would be a liar."

Ibn Abī Mulayka said: "I met thirty of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), all of whom feared hypocrisy for themselves; not one of them would say that he had the faith of Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl."

It is related from al-Ḥasan: "None fears it except a believer, and none feels secure from it except a hypocrite."

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to say to Ḥudhayfa: "I adjure you by Allah, did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) name me to you among the hypocrites?" and he would say: "No, and I will not absolve anyone after you."

I heard our shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "His intention is not 'I do not clear anyone other than you of hypocrisy.' Rather, the intention is 'I will not open this door upon myself, for whoever asks me, "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) name me to you?" I would then be declaring him pure.'"

I say: Close to this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the man who asked him to pray that he be among the seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning: "ʿUkkāsha has preceded you with it."

He did not mean that ʿUkkāsha alone was more entitled to this than the rest of the Companions, but that if he had prayed, another would have stood up, and then another, and the door would have been opened, and perhaps one who did not deserve to be among them would have stood up. So refraining was preferable. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 45, verse 23:

Al-ghishawah (الغشاوة): it is the covering. This covering spread to the eyes from the covering of the heart. What is in the heart of good and evil appears upon the eye, for the eye is the mirror of the heart, showing what is within it. When you intensely hate a man, you dislike his speech and his company, and you find a covering over your eye when you see him and mix with him.

That is the effect of hatred and turning away from him.

The covering (al-ghishawah) was applied to the disbelievers as a punishment for them, for their turning away and their aversion from the Messenger (ﷺ) and from what he brought of guidance and truth. The placing of the covering over them (ʿalā abṣārihim) indicates encompassment over what lies beneath it, like a cloud. And because they were veiled (ghushu) from His remembrance, which He sent down, that veiling became a covering over their eyes, so they do not see the places of guidance.

(Faṣl)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly?﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He knew what would happen before He created him."

He also said: "Upon knowledge that had already preceded with Him."

He also said: "He means the matter that had preceded for him in the Mother of the Book."

Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Muqatil said: "Upon His knowledge concerning him."

Abu Ishaq said: "That is, upon what had preceded in His knowledge, that he is astray, before He created him."

This is what the majority of the exegetes mentioned.

al-Thaʿlabi (al-Thaʿlabi) said: "Upon knowledge from Him of the outcome of his affair."

He said: "It was also said: upon what had preceded in His knowledge, that he is astray before He created him."

Likewise al-Baghawi and Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi mentioned, saying: "Upon His preceding knowledge concerning him, that he will not be guided."

A group of them, including al-Mahdawi and others, mentioned two opinions regarding the verse, of which this is one.

Al-Mahdawi said: "So Allah misguided him upon a knowledge that He had of him, that he does not deserve (guidance)."

He said: "It was also said: upon the knowledge of the worshipper of the idol that it neither benefits nor harms."

According to the first view, ʿalā ʿilm (upon knowledge) is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) referring to the subject (the agent, Allah). The meaning is: Allah misguided him, knowing that he is among the people of misguidance in His preceding knowledge.

According to the second, it is a circumstantial phrase referring to the object: that is, Allah misguided him in a state in which the disbeliever knew that he was astray.

I say: according to the first aspect, the meaning is that Allah misguided him while knowing him, his statements, and what suits him and befits him, and that nothing other than this is fitting for him, before his creation and after it, and that he is fit for misguidance and not fit to be guided, and that if he were guided, He would have placed guidance in other than its place and with one who does not deserve it. The Lord, exalted is He, is Wise, and He places things only in their fitting places.

So the verse, according to this view, includes the affirmation of divine decree and the wisdom for which He decreed misguidance upon him, and it mentions knowledge, since it is what reveals and clarifies the realities of matters, placing things in their proper places, and giving good to one who deserves it and withholding it from one who does not. This does not occur without knowledge. So He, glorified is He, misguided him upon His knowledge of his circumstances that suit his misguidance, require it and call for it. He, glorified is He, often mentions this together with His informing that He misguides the disbeliever, as He said: ﴿Whoever Allah wants to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky. Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe﴾. And He, exalted, said: ﴿He misguides by it many and guides by it many, and He misguides by it none except the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause corruption on earth. Those are the losers﴾. And He, exalted, said: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾; ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾;

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and ungrateful﴾; ﴿And Allah misguides the wrongdoers﴾; ﴿Thus Allah misguides whoever is a transgressor and doubter﴾;

﴿Thus Allah seals the heart of every arrogant tyrant﴾; ﴿Thus Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know﴾. He, glorified is He, has informed that He does this as a punishment for the possessors of these crimes, and this is a second misguidance after the first, as He said: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few﴾. And He, exalted, said: ﴿And what will make you realize that when it [the sign] comes, they will not believe? And We will turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾.

(Faṣl)

In His saying: ﴿And Allah misguided him upon knowledge﴾ there is another view: that it is upon the knowledge of the one who is misguided, as it was said: "upon knowledge from him that his deity neither benefits nor harms." The meaning then is: Allah misguided him along with his knowledge by which the proof is established against him; He did not misguide him in ignorance and lack of knowledge.

This resembles His saying: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know﴾; and His saying: ﴿And He averted them from the way, though they were discerning﴾; and His saying: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them﴾; and His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her by it﴾.

And Moses' saying to Pharaoh: ﴿You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidence﴾; and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons, but a party of them conceal the truth while they know﴾; and His saying: ﴿For they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾; and His saying: ﴿And Allah would not misguide a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid﴾.

Its parallels are many.

According to this estimation, he is astray from the path of his right guidance while seeing it with his own eyes, as in the hadith: "The most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar whom Allah did not benefit by his knowledge."

For the one who strays from the path may follow his desire while knowing that rectitude and guidance lie in opposition to what he does. Since guidance is knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, its opposite is twofold: ignorance, and abandoning acting upon it. The first is misguidance in knowledge, and the second is misguidance in intention and action. The phrase "upon knowledge" occurs in His saying: ﴿And We chose them upon knowledge﴾, in His saying: ﴿And Allah misguided him upon knowledge﴾, and in His saying: ﴿He said, "I was given it only upon knowledge."﴾ In the first, the knowledge there is attributed to Allah, by unanimous agreement.

In the second and third there are two views, and the preferred view regarding His saying ﴿And Allah misguided him upon knowledge﴾ is that it be like the first, and this is the view of the majority of the early scholars.

The third has two possible views, and the reasoning for both has been mentioned.

And Allah knows best. The intent is to mention the levels of qadar (divine decree): knowledge, writing, will, and creation.

(Faṣl)

When you reflect upon the state of those infatuated with images, who are enslaved by them, you will find this verse applying to them, reporting their state.

Some scholars said: "Nothing among beloved things fully occupies the heart's love except the love of Allah, or the love of a human like you. As for the love of Allah, it is that for which the servants were created, and in it lies the ultimate of their happiness and the perfection of their bliss. As for a human like oneself, male or female, there is in him a resemblance and affinity between the lover and him that is not found between him and another category of creatures. Therefore, in loving any beloved other than one of one's own kind, nothing is known that removes the intellect, corrupts perception, and causes the will to be cut off from other than that beloved. Rather, this is known only in love for one's own kind, which fills the heart, captures the mind, and makes him listen and obey his beloved, as it was said:

"Indeed your love that is in my heart
has made me a listener and obedient."

This listening and obedience grows strong in many lovers, until he gives up his soul and surrenders it to destruction in obedience to his beloved, just as the fighter gives his soul to his Lord until he is killed in His way. And if the Prophet, Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said in the hadith related by Ahmad and others:

"The drinker of wine — or he said the habitual drinker of wine — is like a worshipper of idols."

And ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by a group playing chess and said: "What are these images to which you are devoted?"

So what is the assumption about the lover, infatuated and annihilated in his beloved?

For this reason Allah, glorified is He, joined wine with the stone idols (al-anṣāb), which are the idols worshipped besides Allah, saying: ﴿O you who believe, indeed wine, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to occur among you through wine and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90–91].

It is well known that the drunkard's intoxication does not last; rather he must sober up, and perhaps his times of sobriety are more than his times of intoxication.

As for the intoxication of love, its sufferer rarely awakens except when the messengers come calling him to come before Allah, exalted is He.

(Section: On the trickery of Satan with the materialist naturalists, the Dahriyya)

These are a people who stripped created things of their Creator, and they said what Allah has related of them:

﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24].

These are two groups.

One group said: when the Creator, glory be to Him, made the celestial spheres moving with the greatest motion, they revolved upon Him and burned Him, and He was unable to control them or to hold their movements in check.

And another group said: things have no beginning whatsoever; rather, they come out from potentiality into actuality.

So when what was in potentiality comes out into actuality, things come into being, both their compounds and their simples, from their own essence and not from anything else.

They said: the world is eternal, it has never ceased and will never cease, it does not change, and it does not perish. It is not possible for the Originator to perform an act that ceases and perishes unless He ceases and perishes along with His act; and this world is what sustains these parts that are in it.

These are truly the Muʿaṭṭilah (the deniers of divine attributes), and they are the chief figures of the Muʿaṭṭilah. This denial has spread to all the other groups of Muʿaṭṭilah, despite their differing opinions and divergence in denial, just as the disease of shirk (associating partners with Allah) has spread, in its roots and its details, among all groups of polytheists despite their differing doctrines concerning it, and just as the rejection of prophethood has spread, in its roots and its details, among all who rejected prophethood or some attribute of it, or who affirmed it in general while rejecting its purpose and essence or part of it.

These three groups: their disease and affliction have spread among people, and none has been saved from it except the followers of the Messenger, who know the reality of what he brought, who hold fast to it and to nothing else, outwardly and inwardly.

So the disease of denial (taʿṭīl), the disease of associating partners (ishrāk), and the disease of opposing the Messenger and rejecting what he brought, or some part of it, are the root of the world's affliction, the source of every evil, and the foundation of every falsehood.

Thus there is no sect among the people of atheism, falsehood and innovation (bid'ah) except that its doctrine derives from these three roots, or from some of them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 45, verse 29:

Ata' said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of Allah Most High: ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾

Allah wrote the deeds of the children of Adam and what they would do until the Day of Resurrection.

He said: The angels copy down what the children of Adam do day by day, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29].

There is another view regarding the verse: that the angels' copying (istinsakh) is their writing down of what the children of Adam do after they have done it.

It may be said, and this is the most apparent view: the verse encompasses both matters. Allah commands His angels, and they copy from the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab) the deeds of the children of Adam, and then they record them against them when they do them, so they neither add to what they copied from the Mother of the Book the weight of an atom nor subtract from it.

(Section)

Most of the exegetes hold that this copying is from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). The angels copy what will occur of the deeds of the children of Adam before they do them, and they find it in agreement with what they do, so Allah confirms from it what carries reward or punishment and discards what is vain.

Ibn Mardawayh mentioned in his tafsir, through various chains to Baqiyyah, from Artah ibn al-Mundhir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ), that the first thing Allah created was the pen. He took it with His right hand, and both of His hands are right. He wrote the world and what would occur in it of deeds done, of righteousness or wickedness, moist or dry, and He enumerated it at the Reminder. He said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾. Is a copy not made only from something already completed?

Adam said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾.

He said: The guardian angels copy from the Mother of the Book what the children of Adam do, for a person only acts according to what the angel has copied from the Mother of the Book.

In the tafsir of al-Ashja' from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, he said:

Everything that is to occur was written in the Reminder (al-Dhikr) with Him. Then He sent the guardian angels over Adam and his offspring, and all His angels copy from the Reminder what the servants do. Then he recited: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾.

In the tafsir of al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said:

It refers to the deeds of the people of the world, the good deeds and the bad, which descend from the sky every morning and evening, including what befalls a person on that day or night: one who is killed, one who drowns, one who falls from the top of a house, one who plunges from a mountain, one who falls, one who is burned by fire, and they preserve all of that for him.

And when a thing is (recorded), they ascend with it to the sky, and they find it written in the Wise Reminder just as it is in the sky.

(Benefit)

Baqiyy ibn Makhlad said: Sahnun and al-Harith ibn Miskin related to us, from Ibn al-Qasim, from Malik, that he used to frequently say: ﴿We only think it is a mere assumption, and we are not certain﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32].

al-Qa'nabi said: I entered upon Malik ibn Anas during his illness from which he died. I greeted him, then sat down, and I saw him weeping. I said to him: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, what makes you weep?" He said to me: "O son of Qa'nab, why would I not weep? And who has more right to weep than I?

By Allah, I wish that I had been struck with a whip for every issue on which I gave a legal verdict based on ra'y (personal opinion). I had latitude in what others had already preceded me in, and I wish I had not given verdicts based on ra'y."

Ibn Abi Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us, saying: I heard al-Shafi'i say: "The one who examines ra'y and then repents from it is like the madman who was treated until he was cured, and he is at his most rational when the affliction that had seized him has ended."

Ibn Abi Dawud said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: I heard my father say: "You scarcely see anyone who examined ra'y without there being corruption (dakhal) in his heart."

'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad also said: I heard my father say: "A weak hadith is more beloved to me than ra'y." 'Abd Allah said: I asked my father about a man who is in a land where he finds none but a companion of hadith who cannot distinguish its sound from its weak narrations, and companions of ra'y, and a calamity befalls him. My father said: "He should ask the companions of hadith and not ask the companions of ra'y; a weak hadith is stronger than ra'y."

The definite article in "al-sa'ah" (the Hour) is for previous reference, and it is the Hour of Resurrection; that is, the time of resurrection, just as it is expressed by "the Day."

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿wa-al-sa'atu la rayba fiha﴾ with the nominative "al-sa'atu," as a conjunction (ʿatf) with the clause "inna wa'da Allahi haqq" (indeed, the promise of Allah is true).

Hamzah alone read it with the accusative "wa-al-sa'ata," as a conjunction with "inna wa'da Allah," which is conjunction with two objects of one governing element (min al-ʿatf ʿala maʿmulay ʿamilin wahid). The meaning of ﴿ma nadri ma al-sa'ah﴾ is: "we do not know the reality of the Hour." The negation of knowledge of its reality is a kinayah (metonymic implication) for denying the occurrence of the Hour; that is, they knew that it would not occur, relying on imaginings which they thought were proofs, such as their saying: ﴿When we are bones and crumbling dust, shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?﴾ [al-Isra': 49].

As for His saying ﴿in nazunnu illa zannan﴾ (We only think it is a mere assumption), it clearly appears to be connected to what precedes it, their saying ﴿ma nadri ma al-sa'ah﴾ (we do not know what the Hour is), and it is clarified by what follows it, His saying ﴿wa ma nahnu bi-mustayqinin﴾ (and we are not certain). Its position (mawqi') and meaning are problematic, and there is also a difficulty in its composition (nazm). As for the difficulty regarding its position and meaning: the speakers are certain of the non-occurrence of the Hour, because of what was related of their saying just before: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], etc. Therefore it is not correct to say that they assume the occurrence of the Hour in any way at all, not even as a possibility.

(Fa'idah)

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud, when an earthquake struck Kufa: "Your Lord is asking you to make amends (yastaʿtibukum), so make amends to Him (fa-aʿtibūhu)." This is the istiʿtab (seeking to have one's lord's displeasure removed) which He negated in the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿So today they shall not be brought out from it, nor shall they be asked to make amends.﴾

That is: We do not seek from them the removal of Our displeasure (ʿatb) against them, for its removal can only come through repentance (tawbah), and repentance does not benefit in the Hereafter. This is different from the servant seeking his Lord's pleasure, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they ask to have amends made, they will not be among those who are granted it.﴾

Its meaning is: if they seek the removal of Our displeasure against them and pardon, they will not be among those whose displeasure is removed.

That is: they are not among those for whom the displeasure is removed. This istiʿtab benefits in this world, not in the Hereafter.
